title: Grateful Dead Live at Capitol Theater on 1971-02-20
lineage: Jace's DAT (48 KHz) playback on Sony PCM-R500, AES digital output > Benchmark DAC1, XLR analog output > Grace Lunatec V3, sample rate at 96 KHz, AES digiout) > AES digital input, professional mode/sync - LynxTwo soundcard in E6400 dual core processor-based PC > HD as 24 bit/96 KHz WAV > Ozone 3.0 > MBIT+ dithering to 16/44.1 KHz WAV > CDWAV 1.9 (tracking) > FLAC (level 8).   Recording, editing and mastering with Wavelab 5.0.  All cables were Mogami Gold 0.3m pro-audio XLR cables.  All components in the transfer/mastering chain were powered from a Cyberpower 1285AVR noise-attenuated uninterruptible AC power supply.
taper: Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.
source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out > Fostex D5 @ 48 kHz x 2 > WBOTB Master DAT.

ai_review.summary: High‑quality Betty Cantor soundboard with a relaxed yet well‑played show highlighted by a stellar Bird Song, electric Ripple and smoky Lovelight jams.
ai_review.review: The transfer captures a brilliant mix from the famed Cantor tapes, with only occasional dropouts that don’t detract from the overall clarity. Musically the night is laid‑back but tight, delivering standout moments such as the early Cryptical/Other One suite, an electric Ripple, and two superb instrumental breaks in Lovelight, while the second set falters slightly on vocal delivery of Loser.

ai_rating.rationale: Reviews consistently praise a strong performance and mostly excellent soundboard quality; minor dropouts and a few weaker moments keep the rating just above four stars.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Brilliant, lively mix from Betty Cantor source with a crisp transfer; a few annoying dropouts are noted but overall clarity and balance are strong.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is relaxed yet tight, featuring the Cryptical/Other One suite and strong jams; second set dips slightly in vocal precision but still delivers highlights like Johnny B. Goode, Ripple and a memorable Lovelight with extended instrumental sections.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Jangly leads on Me and My Uncle and Hard to Handle; tasteful guitar tone throughout, especially in Bird Song and Ripple.
band_member_comments.Phil: Laser‑focused attack on the Other One intro and brooding movement later in the suite; solid bass foundation despite a laid‑back vibe.
band_member_comments.Bob: Dylanesque vocal passage in Cryptical/Other One; notable singing moments like 'Standing on a Tower' line repeated.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen adds eerie organ fills and an enthusiastic rap on Lovelight, contributing to the song’s two standout instrumental breaks.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann adapts quickly after Mickey's departure, delivering strong drum breaks and driving the groove on both sets.
